scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: The activation–HNRNPLL–PTPRC exon-skipping mechanism is established and biologically coherent in T cells. Its main weakness is overgeneralization from T-cell isoform regulation to variation across all mixed cord-blood immune populations.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: HNRNPLL, activation state, PTPRC exon 4 inclusion or skipping, and reciprocal CD45RO production are integrated into a clear activation-to-splicing-to-surface-epitope mechanism. PTBP1 and the ancillary surface markers remain optional predictions rather than developed parts of the mechanism, while extension from T cells to all mixed cord-blood populations is underexplained. No synthesis ceiling was applied because the principal HNRNPLL-to-CD45RA mechanism is explicit and the relevant contextual features are integrated.
